dxgive.evidence_source: [/2/Text/2] To define "at risk children", Kovacs advises to take a cut-off of 13 in samples where false negatives are not recommendable [35]. In this study, item 9, reflecting "thinking of the dead", was excluded for ethical reasons (see also reference 10). This had implications for the proposed cut-off score of this study, which was therefore reduced to 11.

Source.evidence_source: [/1/Text/15] All children completed a Dutch version of the Children's Depression Inventory (CDI [34, 35], Dutch version by Timbremont & Braet [53]).; [/2/Text/3] Furthermore, all children filled out the Dutch version of the Self-Perception Profile for Children (SPPC [17]; Dutch version by Veerman, Straathof, Ten Brink & Treffers [54]).; [/2/Text/4] A Dutch revision of the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory for Children (STAIC [47]) by Bakker, van Wieringen, van der Ploeg and Spielberger [5] for children aged 8 to 15 was used.

MedCat.evidence_source: [/1/Text/15] The CDI is used for children aged 7 to 17 and includes 27 items measuring cognitive, affective and behavioural symptoms of depression in children.; [/2/Text/3] The SPPC is a 36-item measure for children aged 8 to 12, surveying children's perceived competence across five specific domains – academic competence, social acceptance, athletic competence, physical appearance, behavioural conduct – as well as global self-worth.
MedCat.warning: STAIC measures anxiety, which is not a direct mediator category in the provided list for depression. Therefore, it is not coded for MedCat.
